title: MPs call for reform to help gig venues secure cover
full_text:
MPs call for reform to help gig venues secure cover
The Insurance Council of Australia has welcomed a NSW parliamentary inquiry’s recommendation to investigate law reforms that could improve cover affordability for live music venues and festivals.
The inquiry’s final report, issued last week, found public liability insurance has become a major cost burden across the industry.
It recommends the state work with the federal government and stakeholders to investigate different insurance models and opportunities for reforms, including tort changes, that could help reduce premiums.
“The inquiry’s recommendation should spur the NSW government to work with insurers on reform that maintains protections for injured people while helping make insurance more affordable for the venues and festivals that keep live music playing,” ICA said.
The peak body says rising payouts and legal fees are driving up claim costs and flowing through to premiums.
ICA adds the NSW civil liability framework has not been significantly reformed since 2002 and has failed to keep pace with changes in the way claims are made and litigated.
It has called for caps on legal costs, a ban on claim farming and mandatory mediation.
In its submission to the inquiry in February, ICA said some live music venues were struggling to obtain public liability cover at affordable rates.
It attributed the pressure to rising claim costs, the hard insurance market between 2019 and 2024, and the risks associated with live music venues, including alcohol service, late operating hours, staging and rigging equipment, and a mobile workforce.
ICA said the average cost of public liability insurance increased by 55%-60% between 2019 and 2024, outpacing inflation.
It also pointed to growing physical and psychological injury claims, medical costs and litigation expenses as factors driving premiums.
The ICA submission supported targeted government funding for risk management training and mitigation programs, particularly for smaller venues.
